paper_metadata.title: Preparation and characterization of Mo/ZrO2–Y2O3 composites
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals & Hard Materials

evidence.quote: Mo/ZrO2–Y2O3 composites were successfully prepared through high-energy ball milling and powder metallurgy technique.
Composites with ZrO2 volume fractions of 0, 3, and 5 vol% and corresponding Y2O3 volume fractions of 0, 0.2, and 0.35 vol%, respectively
Composites with ZrO2 volume fractions of 0, 3, and 5 vol%
corresponding Y2O3 volume fractions of 0, 0.2, and 0.35 vol%
Ammonium tetramolybdate [(NH4)2Mo4O13·2H2O] was heated at 520 °C for 4 h in a muffle furnace
sequentially treated by dry milling for 8 h, to convert (NH4)2Mo4O13·2H2O into MoO3

process_steps.input_state: MoO3 powder mixed with Zr(NO3)4·3H2O and Y(NO3)3·6H2O solution

evidence.quote: The prepared solution was mixed evenly with MoO3 powders through wet milling for 8 h. MoO3 composite powders were obtained after drying.
The composite powders were reduced in hydrogen atmosphere at 520 °C for 4 h to convert MoO3 into MoO2.
Then, the Mo/ZrO2–Y2O3 composite powders were obtained by reducing MoO2 to Mo at 960 °C for 5 h.
The composite powders were filled into a rubber can and pressed by cold isostatic pressing (CIP) at 280 MPa for 20 min
sintered in an intermediate frequency induction sintering furnace under H2 atmosphere at 1920 °C for 3 h
The cylindrical sintered compacts were heated for 20 min at 1350 °C in a molybdenum wire furnace (ZMY-50-15)
sequentially subjected to multistep rotary swaging, causing total deformation to exceed 84%
tensile samples were annealed at 800 °C and 1200 °C for 1 h, respectively.
tensile samples were annealed at 800 °C and 1200 °C for 1 h, respectively.
